definition: Succinct means marked by compact precision.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word succinct. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know succinct should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Field manuals prize succinct writing: every word a soldier reads in the rain has to earn its ink.
Brief is the bare stopwatch fact — milder than succinct, because brief only counts the words and makes no promise that anything important survived the cut.
Telegraphic goes further than succinct — words drop out entirely, style pared to stubs, and completeness starts paying the bill.

Compact means much packed into little space, and it is as true of cars and folding chairs as of prose. Succinct is compact applied to wording, with a guarantee attached: everything needed is present, nothing extra. A compact thing saves space; succinct writing saves words without losing content.

Crisp praises the feel of the delivery — brisk, clean, a snap of energy in every line. Succinct praises the ratio instead: full coverage in few words. A crisp reply can still leave something out; a succinct one, by its nature, covers all that matters.
